dietEvidence.body: The broad, squared snout, downturned skull and densely packed dental battery support low-level cropping, but the plants eaten and the exact feeding height are inferred. Tooth replacement is well documented; no gut contents are known, and the soft tissue of the snout is not preserved.

sizeNote: Length and mass are estimates from incomplete material, not measurements of a whole animal.
tagline: A rebbachisaurid with a wide, squared-off snout and a dental battery that replaced teeth rapidly. It likely grazed low vegetation.
summary: A rebbachisaurid with a wide, squared-off snout and a dental battery that replaced teeth rapidly. It likely grazed low vegetation.

discovery.body: Named by Sereno et al., 1999. The holotype, MNN GAD512 (also cited as MNN GDF512), is a partial skull and neck from the Elrhaz Formation, Niger. The mounted skeleton is reconstructed from several individuals.

fossilEvidence.title: Preserved material
fossilEvidence.body: A nearly complete skull and partial skeleton, plus additional material.

fossilEvidence.title: Stratigraphic and geographic occurrence
fossilEvidence.body: Elrhaz Formation, Gadoufaoua records the species in the Early Cretaceous. The numeric range used here is ≈115–110 Ma, an occurrence estimate rather than a direct date on every specimen.

anatomy.title: Preserved anatomy
anatomy.body: The skull is broad and shallow, the jaw carries many small teeth, and the neck is relatively short.

behaviour.body: No nest, trackway or socially associated assemblage is known. The mounted skeleton is reconstructed from several individuals, so it is not a record of one animal’s posture or behaviour. The extensive pneumaticity is direct skeletal evidence, but its respiratory or buoyancy function is inferred.

reconstruction.body: A licensed life reconstruction is assigned to this record and credited in Sources and credits. The species is known from a nearly complete skull and partial skeleton, plus additional material. The reconstruction is an artist's interpretation of appearance, not a direct observation from the fossil record; preserved integument, where present, is described in the anatomy section, and the soft-tissue outline is otherwise inferred.

confidenceNote: Confidence is high for the dental battery, snout shape and pneumatic axial skeleton. It is lower for the catalogue number (MNN GAD512 or GDF512), the reconstructed skull, feeding height, soft tissue and any social behaviour. No gut contents are known.
